newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kazakhstan pledges open trade in bid to join WTO.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan pledges open trade in bid to join WTO.

text.p: Ex-Soviet Kazakhstan, a growing regional power in Central Asia, on Wednesday pushed its bid to win membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) with a pledge that it would follow open trade policies.

The promise was made by the landlocked state's first deputy economy minister Dzhanat Ertlesova at the first session of a WTO working party set up to study the Kazakh application and prepare a text for an eventual agreement on admission.

Trade officials said Ertlesova told the working party her country -- the ninth largest in the world geographically -- would bring its own trade laws into line with WTO rules and would shortly submit an initial offer on market openings in goods and services.

The Kazakh government, officially reported on Tuesday to be pulling out of a customs union with Russia and other former Soviet neighbours arguing it threatened the country's economic progress, was pursuing wide-ranging reforms, she said.

The trade officials said Kazakhstan's reform pledge and an initial report on its foreign trade policies were widely welcomed by key countries in the 130-member WTO, including the United States, the European Union, Canada and Japan.
They applauded its efforts to establish a market economy and build a legal foundation for trade reform, according to the officials.

But the EU and the United States called on the Kazakh government to make a "standstill" commitment, which would prevent it from introducing any measures going against WTO rules while the entry negotiations were in process.
Such a commitment would prevent it implementing tough new policies whose easing could then be used as a bargaining chip for concessions from WTO members in the admission talks.

The two trade powers also asked Kazakhstan, one of 12 former Soviet republics seeking admission to the trade body, to ensure that it observed full transparency on proposed changes to economic and trade laws and regulations.

In 1995 Kazakhstan, rich in mineral resources and a major grain grower, exported goods worth $4.97 billion and its imports totalled $3.74 billion. Russia is its main partner, accounting for some 45 per cent of its foreign trade.

Russia, which under its old Soviet communist rulers scorned the pre-WTO General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) as a capitalist club, is also seeking to join. Talks have been under way for over two years.
China, Kazakhstan's other big neighbour, has been in entry negotiations for a decade.
